purpose: Replace YouTube embed iframes with lightweight static thumbnail placeholders that load the real player on user click, reducing page weight and improving LCP.
riskRationale: The feature is architecturally sound and well-integrated with existing pipelines, but three critical bugs (orphaned </iframe> tag, CSS hiding of <noscript> fallback, corruption of the fallback iframe by the lazy-load pipeline) and several important issues must be fixed before merge. All fixes are straightforward and well-scoped.
breakingChanges: Removes the unused lazyLoadIframes code path from enqueue script logic

text: Well-structured PR that adds a meaningful performance feature with good WordPress integration (filters, exclusion support, nested UI toggle). The code mostly follows existing patterns. However, three critical bugs must be addressed: (1) the regex leaves orphaned </iframe> tags in the output, (2) CSS `noscript { display: none }` hides the non-JS fallback entirely, and (3) the fallback iframe inside <noscript> gets its src stripped when lazyLoadImages is also active. Several important attribute/accessibility gaps in the injected iframe also need attention.

reasoning: Three critical bugs (orphaned HTML, hidden noscript fallback, second-pass regex corruption) and important attribute/accessibility gaps must be fixed before merge. All issues have clear, safe fixes that an automated agent can apply.

message: Clean, focused regex for YouTube URL matching that correctly handles youtube.com, youtube-nocookie.com, and youtu.be variants.

generate_video_placeholder() provides 3 WordPress filters (wppo_video_placeholder_allowed, wppo_video_play_button_html, wppo_video_placeholder_html) for extensibility without the author needing to anticipate every use case.
Solid responsive CSS with aspect-ratio, hover scale effect, and focus-visible keyboard outline for accessibility.
Good UX: the Video Placeholder toggle only appears when Video Lazy Loading is enabled, using a nested field pattern.
Self-guarding init with el.dataset.wppoInit check prevents double-binding, and properly supports both click and keyboard (Enter/Space) activation with preventDefault, meeting WCAG 2.1.1 requirements.
Correctly guards the enqueue by ANDing enableVideoPlaceholder with lazyLoadVideos, matching the backend generation logic and UI nesting.
YouTube placeholder replacement is inserted before the generic lazy-load pass, preventing duplicate processing and correctly falling through to the existing pipeline for non-YouTube iframes.

The regex pattern '#<iframe\b([^>]*?)src=["']([^"']+)["'][^>]*>#is' only matches the opening <iframe ...> tag, NOT the closing </iframe>. When generate_video_placeholder() replaces the match with a <div>, the orphaned </iframe> remains in the HTML output, producing invalid markup.
suggestion: Make the regex match the full <iframe>...</iframe> element (including the closing tag) so the replacement produces clean HTML.

message: 'noscript { display: none; }' breaks the noscript fallback for users with JavaScript disabled. When JS is off, the <noscript> element is in the DOM and its children should render. This CSS rule hides it, making the video completely inaccessible to users without JavaScript.
suggestion: Remove the noscript display:none rule entirely. When JS is enabled, the DOM parser does not render the <noscript> element; when JS is disabled, it must remain visible.

message: The YouTube placeholder pass injects a <noscript><iframe>...</iframe></noscript> inside the placeholder <div>. When lazyLoadImages is also active, the second regex pass matches the iframe inside <noscript> and calls process_iframe_tag() on it, which moves src to data-src. This breaks the no-JS fallback entirely.
suggestion: Protect the noscript iframe from the second regex pass by temporarily replacing all <noscript> blocks with a unique marker before the lazy-load regex runs, then restoring them afterward.

message: The loadVideo() function creates a replacement iframe with only 'allow', 'allowFullscreen', and 'loading' attributes. Original attributes from the embedded iframe (width, height, sandbox, referrerpolicy, frameborder) are lost. The iframe also lacks a 'title' attribute required by WCAG 2.4.1, and the aria-label transferred from the placeholder ('Play video') is semantically incorrect for an iframe.
suggestion: Set width='100%' and height='100%' on the injected iframe to inherit the placeholder's aspect-ratio. Preserve original attributes via data-* attributes on the placeholder. Add a descriptive title attribute for accessibility.

message: loadVideo() can be invoked twice for the same element if both click and keyboard events fire simultaneously. The second call throws a TypeError because el.parentNode is null after the first replaceChild.
suggestion: Add a loaded guard flag checked at the top of loadVideo() to prevent double execution.

message: The injected iframe created by loadVideo() has no error handling. If the YouTube iframe fails to load (network error, blocked domain, etc.), the user sees a blank space with no fallback or retry mechanism.
suggestion: Add an onerror handler to the injected iframe that restores the placeholder UI or displays an error message if the video fails to load.

message: Inline JavaScript in the onerror attribute is blocked by strict Content Security Policy (CSP) headers and uses string concatenation without JavaScript-specific escaping. While esc_url() protects the URL value, mixing PHP string building with JS code in an HTML attribute is fragile.
suggestion: Replace the inline onerror with a data-* attribute and a JS handler in lazyload.js, or use wp_json_encode() on the fallback URL.

message: The exclude_lazy_videos constructor initialization uses '?? \'\'' as fallback for missing excludeVideos, while all other exclude fields in the same constructor use '?? array()'. This inconsistency means an empty string is passed to Util::process_urls() instead of an empty array.
suggestion: Change the fallback value to ?? array() for consistency with the rest of the constructor and better type safety.

message: generate_video_placeholder() re-runs the same YouTube URL regex that was already executed by the caller to validate the URL and extract the video ID. This redundant computation could be avoided.
suggestion: Pass the matched video ID groups from the caller to generate_video_placeholder() as an additional parameter instead of re-running the regex.
